# Schedule reaper and add configuration

## Goal

As an operator, I want the closure script to run periodically and to be
configurable/disable-able, so it works unattended and can be turned off without
editing code (parent AC3 and the configuration constraint).

## Summary

Wire the reaper into the herdr downtime-worker tick (or a documented
equivalent scheduler) and add settings for on/off and the idle threshold.

## Constraints

- Must not double-handle or race the existing `pane-lifecycle.ts` dispatch monitor; both must be idempotent.
- Configuration must be read from the existing herdr/worklog settings surface.
- A reaper exception must not crash the worker.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reaper runs on a periodic tick (default interval documented) inside the downtime worker (or a documented alternative), gated by an `enabled` setting.
- Settings `enabled` (default on) and `idleThresholdMinutes` (default 30) are read from the settings surface and covered by tests (parent AC3).
- Disabling the setting results in zero close calls (asserted).
- A reaper throw/exception is caught and logged; the worker continues (asserted).
- Coexistence with `pane-lifecycle.ts` is tested: a pane already handled by the dispatch monitor is not closed twice (parent constraint).
- Existing downtime-worker tests remain green.

## Minimal implementation

- Add settings keys and defaults in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.
- Invoke the reaper on the worker tick with a guard so overlapping runs cannot occur.

## Dependencies

- Child-process teardown item.

## Deliverables

- Settings additions, worker scheduling wiring, tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — settings keys
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — periodic wiring
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — de-duplication reference
